jobs.description: BERNER pushing the limits – for those who dare moreMaking a choice about your career and your employer is a choice about your future - a future where you will invest your passion and a large portion of your time, energy, and capacity.  Play a key role in ensuring that our products meet applicable legal and regulatory requirements and contribute to maintaining a compliant and market-ready product portfolio. You will combine your scientific or technical background with an interest in regulatory requirements, chemical product data and legislation. From monitoring regulatory developments and assessing product compliance to preparing Safety Data Sheets and maintaining chemical data, you will translate complex requirements into practical solutions for our products and business processes. Join our Product Compliance team and take an active role in securing product conformity while working closely with Product Management, Purchasing, Quality and our suppliers, as well as supporting our customers with product compliance-related topics.YOUR TASKS- Ensure that our products meet applicable legal and regulatory product compliance requirements- Monitor current and upcoming product legislation and assess its impact on different product groups and our portfolio- Assess chemical products regarding applicable regulatory requirements, particularly REACH, CLP, Biocidal Products Regulation, Detergents Regulation, Cosmetic Product Regulation and the Construction Products Regulation- Create, review and maintain Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and ensure their regulatory compliance and quality- Maintain and ensure the quality of chemical, substance and compliance-related product data in relevant systems- Analyse product compositions, classifications and regulatory product information and derive necessary compliance measures- Review supplier documentation, clarify regulatory requirements with suppliers and verify the completeness and plausibility of provided compliance information- Prepare and maintain compliance-related documents, declarations and certificates- Maintain product and compliance data in SAP, PIM and other relevant systems- Work closely with Product Management and Purchasing during the creation and introduction of new products to identify and implement compliance requirements at an early stage- Support Master Data Management in defining and maintaining legally required product information- Support customers and our subsidiaries with product compliance-related questions and provide relevant regulatory documentation and information- Contribute to the implementation of new and changing regulatory requirements as well as the continuous improvement and digitalization of Product Compliance processesYOUR PROFILE- Academic degree or comparable qualification with a scientific, technical or regulatory background, for example in chemistry, chemical engineering, environmental sciences, materials science, life sciences or a related field- Strong analytical skills, a high level of accuracy and a structured, reliable working style- Enjoy working with chemical and technical data as well as complex legal and regulatory requirements- Ideally, knowledge of European chemical and product legislation, particularly: - REACH Regulation- CLP Regulation- Biocidal Products Regulation- Detergents Regulation- Construction Products Regulation- Cosmetic Product Regulation- Knowledge of PPE legislation is an advantage- Experience in creating and maintaining Safety Data Sheets is an advantage- Experience with SDS authoring via chemical compliance software such as Chemdox is an advantage- High affinity for data and confidence in handling and maintaining larger amounts of technical and regulatory product information- Confident user of Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint- Experience with SAP, PIM systems or comparable product data systems is an advantage- Strong communication and teamwork skills and confidence in collaborating with different business functions, suppliers, customers and external partners- Good English skills; German or additional European language skills are an advantage WHY BERNER? - Job bike leasing (JobRad)  - Commuting allowance  - Wellpass membership & corporate benefits  - Company pension scheme  - Opportunities for further training  - Technically modern equipped workplace  - Company restaurant in Künzelsau or meal vouchers in Cologne  - Attractive conditions for our products in the BERNER online shop Apply Now – We’re Excited to Meet You! Please submit your application via our online form, including your availability and salary expectations. The BERNER Group is a European trading company serving professionals in the mobility, construction, and industrial sectors. We are the leading B2B specialist and an innovative manufacturer of chemical products. Our purpose is: “We are pushing the limits of the possible for the shapers of a better tomorrow.” With our strong brands - BERNER, BTI by BERNER, and CCS - we empower our customers to keep their businesses running successfully. Join our team and shape the future with us! The BERNER Group as employer, dare to differentiate ourselves and provide every employee the opportunity to and enable them to dare to be more.  Together, we push our own limits and contribute to shape a better tomorrow.

jobs.description: IRC (International Rescue Committee) Germany is seeking aProgram Development & Award Advisor (d/f/m), Latin America- in Berlin, or remote (within Germany) | as soon as possible- in part-time (20 hours/week), increase to full-time in the future might be possible (contingent upon funding) | initially for 2 yearsAbout UsFounded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. In 2016, IRC Germany was founded and engages in global humanitarian work as well as throughout Germany in the areas of education, economic wellbeing, and safety, legal protection, and empowerment.IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department (CRRD) runs humanitarian relief, recovery, and development programs focused on safety, health, education, economic well-being, and people’s power to influence decisions, with particular attention to women and girls. Its Awards Management Unit (AMU) secures and manages government donor funding, bridging donors and country programs while ensuring compliance and managing risk. In Latin America and the Caribbean, the IRC responds to crises in Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico, Central America, and Haiti, supporting displaced and host communities through local partners and direct implementation. The Program Development and Award Advisor (PDAA) provides pre- and post-award support to country offices, ensures donor and IRC compliance, leads donor deliverables, and manages donor relationships.Major Responsibilities- Strategic Business Development: support country offices in advancing strategic business development planning efforts, donor engagement, intelligence gathering, positioning and capture. Prepare for and participate in donor meetings, engagement calls, and strategic discussions as needed. - Proposal development: provide quality assurance and quality compliance support on proposals, leading proposal development and coordination as needed. Ensure responsiveness to and compliance with solicitation documents and with IRC’s requirements and policies. - Award portfolio management: manage a portfolio of awards and act as the first point of contact for country award staff on compliance issues. Review agreements and lead negotiation of award terms and conditions with donor counterparts. - Partnerships: guide country offices in managing local and international partners in line with IRC’s PEERs system, and review and process sub-grant agreements. - Monitoring: monitor projects to ensure progress against objectives and compliance with donor guidelines and IRC internal requirements. Monitoring awards can take the shape of monitoring visits, participation in routine meetings and other regular calls. - Experience writing, reviewing and editing funding proposals and other donor deliverables and excellent attention to detail.- Excellent written and oral communication skills, including experience in speaking on relevant issues with internal and external audiences.- English and Spanish language skills at C1-level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CERF) (https://www.europaeischer-referenzrahmen.de/) . Additional knowledge of French and/or German highly desirable.- Solid organizational and creative problem-solving skills: ability to be flexible and work well under pressure in a fast-paced multi-tasking team environment- Excellent IT skills (Word, Outlook, Excel)- Ability and willingness to travel internationally (up to 15 %)- Reporting: provide timely support on narrative reporting, amendments, and modifications. Ensure timely submission of high-quality donor deliverables.- Donor liaison: manage donor relationships on contractual issues, compliance queries and approvals, and represent IRC externally at events and meetings.- Capacity building: mentor Grants and Partnerships staff, develop and deliver training, and support recruitment and onboarding of new team members.- Other duties: contribute to AMU and regional strategic priorities, work with communications teams on donor communication products, and maintain checklists and work processes and systems. Your Profile- Significant work experience in award management or business development with EU donors, particularly ECHO, and other public donors. Experience with and a strong understanding of institutional donors’ compliance requirements.- Two years of international field experience highly desirable, familiarity with countries in the region preferred.- Excellent interpersonal & communication skills: ability to successfully and effectively liaise with people within and across departments in a multi-cultural environment.- Good financial management and budgeting skills- Ability to analyze and synthesize information, work collaboratively as part of a diverse team, handle complex tasks, and work independently We Offer- Meaningful work within a collaborative team- A starting salary between 32.000 and 33.500 Euro gross per year (for part-time, 20 hours/week) as well as an annual salary increase- Attractive employee benefits such as gym membership, company pension scheme, shopping vouchers, childcare subsidy, job bike leasing, subsidized Deutschlandticket (national public transport), and access to timely and confidential psychological support if needed- 30 days of annual leave and special leave days- Flexible hybrid-work options (working hours, office/homebased)- Training and professional development opportunities, including access to free language courses- Assistance services for people with disabilities, if required.We look forward to receiving your application (including CV and – if available – three references) via our application portal (https://theirc.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/de-DE/External_Careers/job/Berlin-Germany/Program-Development---Award-Advisor--d-f-m---Latin-America_JR00006189) – even if you do not meet all the listed requirements. For questions, please contact Friederike Haarbrücker (HR.Deutschland@rescue.org (https://mailto:HR.Deutschland@rescue.org) ).As an organization committed to an empowering work environment, equal opportunities, and against any form of discrimination, we welcome applications from people regardless of their origin, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disabilities, age, or other characteristics protected by applicable law. We particularly encourage people with personal or family experience of flight and migration to apply.With equal qualifications, we give preference to applications from people with severe disabilities. If you have any questions about accessible applications or inclusion, please feel free to contact our Inclusion Officer, Christine Mader (christine.mader@rescue.org (https://mailto:christine.mader@rescue.org) ).To ensure equal opportunities, we kindly ask you to refrain from including photos in your application documents.There is no specific application deadline for this job posting. The position needs to be filled as soon as possible and will remain posted until filled.All IRC workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct (https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct) . On this basis, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding (https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding) , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.You can find more information about IRC Germany at IRCDeutschland.org (https://www.irc-deutschland.org/) .Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: "Taking the pulse of our Earth to safeguard a habitable planet."For section 2.1 "Physics of Earthquakes and Volcanoes" (https://www.gfz.de/en/section/physics-of-earthquakes-and-volcanoes/overview) (department “Geophysics (https://www.gfz.de/en/geophysics) ”), we are looking for a:Research scientist (f_m_x) - SeismologyReference Number 11691Earthquakes induced by human activities, such as deep geothermal energy production, can cause ground shaking that raises concerns among local communities. Understanding earthquake source processes and predicting the resulting ground motions, including their uncertainties, are important for assessing seismic impacts and supporting transparent communication with stakeholders.Within the BMWE-funded collaborative project "Seismological Analysis and Societal Relevance of Deep Energy Projects (SAURIER)", GFZ is responsible for the subproject "TRansparent Interpretation and Characterisation of Earthquake RAdiation Patterns through probabilistic moment TensOr inversion and PGV Simulations (TRICERATOPS)". We are looking for a motivated researcher with a strong background in seismology and experience in earthquake source analysis and seismic waveform processing.The successful candidate will contribute to developing and applying probabilistic methods for earthquake source characterisation and physics-based ground motion modelling. The research will focus on quantifying the influence of earthquake source parameters and subsurface structure on predicted ground motions and their uncertainties, with the aim of estimating seismic impact zones.Fraunhofer IEG coordinates SAURIER and brings together seismological and social science research to improve the assessment and communication of induced seismicity.Your responsibilities:- Analyse seismic waveform datasets and determine earthquake source parameters, particularly for small to moderate earthquakes, using probabilistic methods including uncertainty quantification- Integrate earthquake source parameters and their uncertainties into physics-based ground motion simulations using numerical modelling tools such as Pyrocko and its Green's function modelling framework- Investigate the sensitivity of predicted ground motions to source parameters, including focal mechanism, source depth and rupture characteristics, as well as subsurface structure- Develop and validate probabilistic ground motion models for moderate earthquakes and contribute to the estimation of seismic impact zones- Develop, test and document scientific software and reproducible analysis workflows- Develop clear and accessible visualisations of earthquake source characteristics, probabilistic ground motion simulations and estimated seismic impact zones for different target groups, including scientists, authorities and the general public, in collaboration with social science partners at UFZ- Collaborate with project partners and contribute to the interpretation and communication of scientific results- Publish research results in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present findings at national and international conferences- Contribute to project reports, meetings and scientific outreach activitiesAbout You:Essential Qualifications:- A Master's degree (MSc) and a PhD in Earth Science, with a focus on seismology and geophysics- Solid geophysical and seismological background- Experience in local earthquake analysis, including moment tensor inversion- Good programming skills in Python, experience in scientific data processing, and experience in developing, adapting and validating computational methods for seismological research, including the implementation of reproducible workflows in Python- Familiarity with seismology toolboxes (e.g. Pyrocko, ObsPy) and visualisation tools (e.g. GMT, ParaView, QGIS)- Experience in scientific research, demonstrated through a convincing and strong publication record, software contributions and other research outputs appropriate to career stage- Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate scientific results clearly- Experience in collaborative and externally funded research projectsDesirable Qualifications:- Experience in numerical seismic wave propagation or ground motion modelling- Knowledge of probabilistic inversion methods, uncertainty quantification or sensitivity analysis- Experience with induced seismicity and analysis of moderate earthquakesStart date: 1st April 2027Fixed-term: 24 MonateSalary: Die Stelle ist nach TVöD Bund mit der Entgeltgruppe 13 bewertet. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt nach den tariflichen Bestimmungen und den entsprechenden persönlichen Voraussetzungen.Working hours: Teilzeit 50% (derzeit 19,50 h/Woche)Place of work: PotsdamWhat we offer:- Ambitious and varied tasks in a dynamic and international research environment- State-of-the-art equipment- Public service benefits- Extensive training opportunities- Professional career advice offered by our in-house Career-Centre- Flexible working hours and conditions- Support with finding a good work-life balance offered by benefit@work- Institute day-care centre on siteHave we piqued your interest?If so, we look forward to receiving your application by 9th December 2026. Please use our online application form only.Required documents: letter of motivation, CV, academic degree certificates/gradesThe GFZ actively promotes diversity and equal opportunities. We explicitly welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of ethnic and social origin, nationality, gender, sexual orientation and identity, religion/belief, age, and physical or neurodiverse abilities.“Diversity in perspectives” is one of GFZ's core values. As an integral part of supporting diversity at our centre, we actively promote women in science and in leadership positions. To know more about our Diversity policies, contact the diversity team. If you need more information about our gender equality policies, please do not hesitate to contact our Equal Opportunities Officer (https://www.gfz.de/en/career/the-gfz-as-an-employer/employee-representation) and check our Equal Opportunities Plan & Cascade Model (https://www.gfz.de/en/career/the-gfz-as-an-employer/equal-opportunities) .We look forward to applications from people who enjoy working in diverse teams, where everyone feels respected and valued and can fully develop their own talents. Applicants with severe disabilities and equalised persons will receive preferential consideration if equally qualified.Data protection information for applicants (https://www.gfz.de/en/career/job-offers#c95430)In case of any further queries regarding the field of activity, please contact Dr. Daniela Günther (daniela.guenther@gfz.de) via email. jobs.occupation: Research Scientist (m/f/d) in Archaeo- and Palaeogenomics (Tenure Track) (Archäologe/Archäologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN)  headquartered in Frankfurt am Main is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Centre for Human Evolution and Palaeoenvironment (SHEP) in Tübingen  as soon as possibleResearch Scientist (m/f/d) in Archaeo- and Palaeogenomics (Tenure Track)(full time / part time)Location:TübingenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options availableType of contract: The position is initially offered on a fixed-term basis. The type and duration of the contract will depend on the successful candidate’s individual qualifications and profile, as well as the applicable legal framework, and may not exceed six years. Subject to a positive evaluation, the position is intended to lead to a permanent appointment under the Senckenberg tenure track scheme.Remuneration:  collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E 13﻿The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level. The Senckenberg Centre for Human Evolution and Palaeoenvironment (SHEP) is based in Tübingen, Baden-Württemberg.Since 2009, our scientists in Tübingen have been conducting research on the biological and cultural evolution of humans in their environments in close cooperation with the Eberhard-Karls-University of Tübingen.Your Responsibilities- Developing, planning and conducting archaeogenetic and palaeogenetic research projects within the framework of the SHEP research programme in Tübingen- Analysing ancient human DNA, particularly from Eurasia, and reconstructing the evolutionary and population history of ancient human populations- Investigating population structures, kinship patterns and forms of social organisation through the integration of genomic, archaeological and historical data- Scientifically coordinating the generation of new genomic data in collaboration with project partners, and contributing to the development and enhancement of bioinformatic analysis pipelines- Publishing research findings in international peer-reviewed journals, developing research proposals and contributing to third-party funding acquisition- Establishing and maintaining national and international research collaborations, and working closely with research groups at SHEP and the University of Tübingen- Providing academic and professional supervision to staff, as well as supervising doctoral researchers and students- Undertaking organisational responsibilities and coordinating collaborative research activities within the research groupYour Profile- A completed PhD in Archaeogenetics, Evolutionary Biology, Molecular Anthropology, Population Genetics or a related natural science discipline- Strong expertise in the analysis and interpretation of genomic data, particularly ancient DNA, combined with excellent bioinformatic skills- Proven experience in integrating genomic data with archaeological, anthropological and historical evidence- Knowledge of approaches to reconstructing population structures, kinship relationships and forms of social organisation in past communities- Experience in developing and applying genomic or bioinformatic methods; experience in developing computational pipelines would be an advantage- A strong academic publication record, including publications in internationally recognised peer-reviewed journals- Experience in planning, conducting or coordinating scientific research projects, together with the ability to independently develop research proposals and secure third-party funding- Experience in supervising students and early-career researchers- Excellent communication and collaboration skills, together with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research- Excellent written and spoken English, and a willingness to learn German** Desirable skills**- Research expertise in the genomics of early humans, particularly archaic hominins such as Neanderthals.- In-depth knowledge of the demography, population structure and evolutionary history of prehistoric human populations, particularly European hunter-gatherers.- Established national and international research collaborations in archaeogenetics and palaeogenomics.We offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply, as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please submit your complete application, including a cover letter, a research and development plan outlining how you intend to advance the research activities, a detailed CV, academic certificates and employment references, a list of publications and, where available, letters of recommendation, as a single PDF file via our careers portal https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/ by20December 2026.﻿**Please understand that we accept applications exclusively through our careers page. **ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Cosimo Posth at cosimo.posth@senckenberg.de.﻿If you have any questions about the application process, please feel free to contact us at recruiting@senckenberg.de.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/.﻿For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de.
